source: Order adapted from the Daily Turkish deck: each lemma of its ranked list (itself adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, CC BY-SA 4.0, built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus) was matched by meaning to its usual Turkmen equivalent, then edited by hand: film-dialogue words dropped or moved down, Turkish lemmas that share one Turkmen word merged, everyday Turkmen words added where their use would put them. Ranks are an editorial estimate, not a Turkmen corpus count. The ranked list is scripts/turkmen/tm-wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkmen/TM-PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

ex.en: My father met the guests at the airport.
I had coffee instead of tea.

cards.note: After a noun in the genitive: *çaýyň ýerine*. With a person it takes their ending: *meniň ýerime* (instead of me), *seniň ýeriňe* (instead of you).

ex.en: Aýna goes to the market every Saturday.
This book is very interesting.

cards.note: p becomes b before a vowel: *kitaby*, *kitabym* (my book).

ex.en: We saw our friend off.

cards.note: t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýar*: *ugradýar*, *ugradyp*; it stays before a consonant: *ugratdy*.

ex.en: The children are hungry. Is dinner ready?
The train is faster than the bus.
The Karakum is a big desert.
Is this seat free?
His girlfriend lives in Dashoguz.
At last the bus came.
I have four brothers and sisters.

cards.note: Its vowel is long, so t becomes d before a vowel: *dördünji* (fourth).

ex.en: There are a lot of camels in the Karakum.
I said hello to the teacher.

en: to put up (a yurt, a tent)

ex.en: They're building a new school in the village.
I said goodbye to my friends.
Batyr has a big dog.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *bellär*, *belläp*.

ex.en: There's a math test tomorrow.
This carpet was woven by Merjen.

cards.note: Mostly in writing, with a passive verb (*dokaldy*, was woven).

ex.en: I waited an hour and a half.
This phone costs two thousand manat.

In spring we plant tomatoes in the garden.

This sofa is very comfortable.
Which colour are you choosing?
I'll call you this evening.

cards.note: *etmek* changes t to d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *jaň edýär*, *jaň eder*.

ex.en: Let me introduce you to my friend.
Put a little sugar in the tea.
The children are lying on the mattress.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *düşegi*.

ex.en: Wait a second!

ex.tk: Bu dükanda çaýyň köp görnüşi bar.
ex.en: This shop has many kinds of tea.
This shirt is too expensive.

Has the pain gone?

I invited my friends to the wedding.
There are a lot of trees around the building.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *töweregi*, *töwereginde* (around it).

ex.en: This Turkmen song is very beautiful.
Sometimes I walk to work.

ex.tk: Irden ýüzümi sowuk suw bilen ýuwýaryn.
ex.en: In the morning I wash my face with cold water.
Her eyes are brown.

The child can count to ten.

There are eighty houses in the village.
This building has ninety rooms.
It's warm today.
In the evenings it's cool in the mountains.

en: to manage (to do), to cope with

ex.en: She managed the job.
I saw a flock of sheep in the mountains.
The driver stopped the car in front of the house.
A strong wind blew yesterday.
The children picked apples in the garden.
We live on the second floor.
After the meal I washed the dishes.
In the desert the air is hot and dry.
My dad cooks pilaf on Saturdays.
Go up, your room is on the fifth floor.

cards.note: Its last y drops before a case ending: *ýokarda* (above, upstairs), *ýokardan* (from above).

ex.en: They have a good relationship.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *gatnaşygy*.

ex.en: The library is on the third floor.
The pupil put up her hand.
It will probably rain tomorrow.

This apple is sour.
This soup is too salty.

cards.note: Its vowel is long, so t becomes d before a vowel: *ýurdy*, *ýurdumyz* (our country).

ex.en: This singer is very famous.
It's a secret, don't tell anyone!
Merv is an ancient city.
There are five provinces in Turkmenistan.
This is a Turkmen national dish.
This horse is very fast.

cards.note: Its vowel is short, so t stays before a vowel: *aty*, *atym* (my horse). *At* (name), with a long vowel, gives *ady*, *adym*.

ex.tk: Biziň toparymyzda on iki talyp bar.
ex.en: There are twelve students in our group.
Ashgabat's international airport is big.
The sky is clear, it won't rain.
We ate at a local restaurant.

ex.tk: Men her gün sagat altyda turýaryn.
ex.en: I get up at six every day.
In spring there are lots of flowers in the mountains.
In summer it's very hot in Ashgabat.
In autumn there are lots of melons at the market.
In winter it snows in Dashoguz.
We cooked a special meal for the guests.
Everyone danced at the wedding.
The shepherd looks after sheep.

On the road, safety comes first.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *howpsuzlygy*.

en: to rest, to have a rest

ex.en: On Saturday I rested at home.
Call any time.
Fruit is good for your health.
My ear hurts.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *gulagy*, *gulagym* (my ear).

ex.en: That's very strange.
We have two cows in the village.
They have a little daughter.
The child hid his toy.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *gizlär*, *gizläp*.

ex.en: Press the button.
The weather's pleasant in the evening.
Trust matters in a friendship.

Don't hurry, we have time.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *yşygy*.

ex.en: I've lost my key.

It's hot, don't touch!
The doctor works at the hospital.

en: pilaf, plov (rice with meat and carrots)

ex.en: They cook pilaf at weddings.
Ashgabat is a beautiful city.

cards.note: A little more literary than *owadan*.

ex.en: There are five children in this family.

cards.note: More formal than *çaga*: someone's sons and daughters.

ex.en: This film is very funny.
I woke up at seven in the morning.
There are ten girls in our class.
This bag is light.
This answer is wrong.

en: to be glad, to be pleased

ex.en: The children were happy about the snow.
Are you mad? It's freezing outside!

cards.note: Informal, and rude when said about someone.

ex.en: Too much sugar is bad for your health.
There's a big red carpet in the room.
A kilo of potatoes, please.
Do you have a cold drink?
I bought tomatoes and cucumbers at the market.

ex.tk: Aşgabatda bir milliondan gowrak adam ýaşaýar.
ex.en: More than a million people live in Ashgabat.

en: gutap (thin fried pastry with a filling)

ex.en: We had gutap in the evening.

cards.note: p becomes b before a vowel: *gutaby*.

ex.en: In winter the days are short.

Börek is really tasty.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *böregi*.

ex.en: Guess what I've brought!

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *sapagy*, *sapaga*.

ex.en: The truck is carrying bricks.
In summer we eat a lot of watermelon.

cards.note: Respectful and a little formal. Day to day, people say *aýalym* (my wife) or *ärim* (my husband).

ex.en: I have a nine-year-old little brother.

My dad plays the dutar.

en: bagshy (singer of songs and epics with the dutar)

ex.en: A bagshy sang at the wedding.

cards.note: Its second vowel drops before a vowel: *agzy*, *agzym* (my mouth).

ex.en: Put a period at the end of the sentence.

ex.tk: Bu jaýyň diwarlarynda gadymy nagyşlar bar.

ex.tk: Bar eken, ýok eken, bir patyşa bar eken.

ex.tk: Ol garry adam, oňa kömek et.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *äýnegi*.

ex.en: Please speak slowly.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *ýüzügi*.

ex.en: On Monday I go to work.
